description: bench-parse mix28k.toml N=16 MS 147 SUM 444080 (27755/op). parse OK SUM 2834622309 BYTES 27755. flat1600 160.8 ms/op, nest800 112.5, dot800 128.5, flat3200 601. bend PROOF.bend prints All terms check.

Presence map VIx in the row list, miss skips the scan, hit falls back to get. flat1600 ~7 ms/op vs 157, nest800 ~76 vs 115, dot800 ~91 vs 133, mix28 ~11 vs 9.2. Checksums matched. Discard: walk_put_at_head requires VPair<>rows, and seal_puts_newest_last requires a VIx head to survive seal, which would change the rendered document.
rows.repl shares an unchanged suffix but still walks every row (dup + scan). mix28 MS 147/16, flat1600 155.8, nest800 135.3 vs 112.5, dot800 127.8. Checksums matched. Slower on the nested document.

rows.repl stops at the first hit and shares the tail. nest800 48.3 vs 112.5, mix28 7.88, flat1600 156, dot800 131. Checksums matched on unique-key docs. Not equal to rows.repl when the name occurs again later, so header_defines_implicit_table would not keep its old meaning.

Split a long table in half and search both halves in parallel (@unsafe). flat3200 714 vs 601, flat1600 192 vs 161, nest800 125 vs 112, mix28 10.9. Checksums matched. Slower, and the bench no longer prints a bare All terms check.

rows.find calls the tail directly instead of allocating a closure (@unsafe). Sound: duplicate of an old key and of the newest key are both BAD. flat3200 539 vs 601, mix28 N=32 MS 302 (9.44 ms/op) vs 9.13. The ~23k document did not drop. Unsafe fails the proof gate's first line.

Direct rows.look plus heads.or as a thunk so a hit does not scan the rest. dot800 159.5 vs 128.5 (slower: misses pay for the thunk), nest800 108.5 vs 112.5, flat3200 544, mix28 8.9. Checksums matched.

Direct rows.find bounded by a length fuel, but each row spent two fuel units and the rest returned Miss. flat3200 297 vs 601, mix28 12.4. 200 unique keys then a repeat of k0000 parsed OK; the tip parses that file BAD duplicate key.
